To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
supernatants from cultured guinea pig lymphocyte cultures contain a substance that releases serotonin from rabbit platelets.
the 5-hydroxytryptamin (5-HT)-releasing activity is a property of supernatants from guinea pig spleens lymphocytes and that the activity is dependent on molecular weight.
the 5-HT releasing activities of supernatants of cultivated lymphocytes from guinea pigs and the cell migration stimulating activities are similar in their molecular weight range.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a possible involvement of 5-HT in DTH reactions.
the question whether the lymphocyte supernatant contains a factor which is able to release 5-HT and/or to activate the thrombocytes.
a possible role of the 5-HT system in the pathogenesis of DTH reactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
5-HT is involved in the mechanism of DTH reactions.
5-HT releasing and cell migration stimulating activities are two separate activities, but both may be produced in the same supernatant.
the supernatant of stimulated lymphocytes possesses a 5-HT releasing factor which is not the same as the migration stimulating factor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 5-HT releasing factor is identical with the cell migration stimulating factor.
the supernatants of cultivated mixed lymphocytes have a 5-HT releasing effect on rabbit thrombocytes, which is not dependent on Con A stimulation.
supernatants of stimulated and non-stimulated lymphocytes are active in DTH reactions and in the release of 5-HT from rabbit thrombocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
5-HT releasing factors are produced by lymphocytes.
